samples.question: Three separate networks are drawn on white paper, one in each third of the picture: left, centre and right, kept apart by two pale vertical rules. In every network the grey wires meet only at the round dark hubs, and each wire joins exactly two hubs. A network can be DRAWN IN ONE STROKE when a pen can start at some hub of that network, travel only along its wires, draw every one of its wires exactly once and never lift off the paper; the pen may pass through a hub as often as it likes, may never run along the same wire twice, and may never jump from one hub to another without a wire. Exactly one of the three networks can be drawn in one stroke. Which network is it - left, centre or right?
